correctness.rationale: For each cell the self-consistency denominator 1+c(1-e^{-alpha theta}) is strictly positive, yielding a unique state. Exact variation-of-constants integration derives M0, Mtheta and P; the completed square gives P>-r>-1. A quadratic with positive leading term and negative constant has exactly one positive root at P=1. Exact numerator zeros yield two extinction gains for every 0<theta<1. A derivative with respect to the sample phase proves monotonic stability budget; asymptotic expansion at theta=1 yields the coefficient 1+exp(alpha). Every between-mesh state is bounded by a fixed cell propagation factor times its mesh state, completing global physical-time stability/instability. Exact fractional witness and 1250 supplementary random derivative tests pass; computation is not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The model interpolates naturally between a retarded sampled controller and the classical alternating advanced-retarded equation in the 2026 generalized-sampling class. Its complete phase/gain classification identifies two distinct gain settings that annihilate any initial condition exactly after respectively one or two physical units, proves that the entire admissible gain budget grows strictly with advancing the second sample, and quantifies its singular reciprocal divergence at the known endpoint. This is substantive information about feedback stability and finite-time control that is not entailed by sufficient Lipschitz bounds or an isolated numerical example.
